title: Why Use a MARISA Trie from DuckDB?
description: Pack a column of strings into a single BLOB and answer membership, autocomplete, and longest-prefix questions against it — in time proportional to the search key, not the dictionary size. Pairs well with [`bitfilters`](/products/extensions/bitfilters): both answer set-membership questions, but a [MARISA trie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trie) keeps the strings and supports prefix queries.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Big static string sets — wordlists, place names, route prefixes, autocomplete dictionaries — compiled into one self-contained BLOB you can store in any DuckDB column, persist to Parquet, and ship anywhere DuckDB runs.

bulletPoints.label: Autocomplete and type-ahead
bulletPoints.description: Microsecond "starts with" lookups against a single BLOB. Drop a search box on a static corpus without standing up Elasticsearch.

bulletPoints.label: Spell-check and dictionary membership
bulletPoints.description: Exact "is this string in the set?" tests, smaller than a hash set and prefix-aware in a way [`bitfilters`](/products/extensions/bitfilters) can't be.

bulletPoints.label: Longest-prefix-match routing
bulletPoints.description: Find every dictionary string that is itself a prefix of the input — the primitive behind URL routers, CIDR label tables, and rule-matching lookups.

bulletPoints.label: A compact join side
bulletPoints.description: One trie per partition / day / tenant ships dramatically smaller than the equivalent string list, and serves membership and prefix queries from the same blob.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: MARISA is a [succinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succinct_data_structure) static [Patricia trie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radix_tree) maintained as [`s-yata/marisa-trie`](https://github.com/s-yata/marisa-trie); this extension is a thin DuckDB wrapper.

bulletPoints.label: One aggregate produces one BLOB
bulletPoints.description: Aggregate a `VARCHAR` column once at write time and you get a single immutable BLOB. Store it anywhere DuckDB stores BLOBs — table column, Parquet file, S3 object.

bulletPoints.label: Lookup cost scales with the key, not the dictionary
bulletPoints.description: The first query is as fast as the millionth, whether the trie holds a thousand strings or ten million.

bulletPoints.label: Prefix-rich data compresses sharply
bulletPoints.description: URLs, paths, and dictionary words share heavy prefix structure — a 470K-entry English wordlist fits in roughly 800 KB, about a fifth the size of the same words as a flat sorted list.

sections.title: When to choose something else
sections.description: MARISA is a sharp, narrow tool. Knowing where it isn't the right fit is half the value.

bulletPoints.label: Static — no incremental insert or delete
bulletPoints.description: Once built, the trie is immutable. Updates mean rebuilding from the source set.

bulletPoints.label: String keys only
bulletPoints.description: `VARCHAR` in, `VARCHAR` out. Numeric keys need to be encoded as text upstream or stored in a different index.

bulletPoints.label: Unrelated random strings: pick a Bloom
bulletPoints.description: Without shared prefixes, the compression edge disappears. For pure membership on uncorrelated keys, [`bitfilters`](/products/extensions/bitfilters) is smaller and just as fast — but it can't return the strings or answer prefix queries.

useCases.title: Autocomplete backend in SQL
useCases.description: Build the trie once at ingest time, store the BLOB, and serve type-ahead requests directly from DuckDB. No separate search service for static dictionaries.

useCases.title: Spell-check shipped inside a Parquet file
useCases.description: A wordlist or term list compiled into a single BLOB column. Pair with [`fuzzycomplete`](/products/extensions/fuzzycomplete) or [`rapidfuzz`](/products/extensions/rapidfuzz) for fuzzy fallbacks when exact lookup misses.

useCases.title: Routing and longest-prefix-match tables
useCases.description: URL paths, feature-flag rules, geo / CIDR labels — anywhere you ask "which rules match this input?"

useCases.title: Compact join dictionary
useCases.description: One trie per partition or per day. The BLOB ships smaller than the underlying string list and serves prefix and membership queries from the same blob.
